extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, poets, and readers interested in aesthetics and the philosophy of taste
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical inquiry into the origin of our ideas of the Sublime and the Beautiful, with methodological guidance for examining taste and detailed analytical categories (novelty, pain/pleasure, terror, obscurity, magnitude, etc.). Useful for writers, critics, and students evaluating or producing works that aim at the sublime or the beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious method: examine distinct ingredients one by one
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering any complex matter, we ought to examine every distinct ingredient in the composition, one by one; and reduce everything to the utmost simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author advocates a careful, almost timorous approach to inquiry rather than sweeping generalizations; break complex phenomena into simple components before re-composing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examine principles by effects and composition by principles
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought afterwards to re-examine the principles by the effect of the composition, as well as the composition by that of the principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test principles against the results they produce and test composite phenomena back against the basic principles to ensure mutual consistency and explanatory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparison widely (with similar and contrary things)
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to compare our subject with things of a similar nature, and even with things of a contrary nature; for discoveries may be, and often are made by the contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The greater number of comparisons made, the more general and certain our knowledge is likely to prove; contrast can reveal distinctions that single examples miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce to induction and experiment where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory founded on experiment, and not assumed, is always good for so much as it explains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build theories from observed facts and experiments; inability to extend a theory indefinitely is not, by itself, a refutation if it explains real phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed cautiously—do not overreach
rubrics_metrics.description: We must not attempt to fly, when we can scarcely pretend to creep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit claims to what can be supported by careful analysis; avoid extravagant or prematurely broad assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit style to matter; prioritize clarity over elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: We must often submit the style to the matter, and frequently give up the praise of elegance, satisfied with being clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing about complex aesthetic principles, clarity of exposition is more important than rhetorical flourish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame objections to premises or conclusions, not isolated examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections ought to be proposed, either to the several principles as they are distinctly considered, or to the justness of the conclusion which is drawn from them; it is improper to produce, as an objection, some poetical passage which does not seem easily accounted for upon the principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique theories by engaging their stated principles or derived conclusions rather than by citing individual poetic passages that might be atypical or due to other causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: inquiry into origin of ideas only
rubrics_metrics.description: The inquiry went no farther than to the origin of these ideas. If the qualities which I have ranged under the head of the Sublime be all found consistent with each other, and all different from those which I place under the head of Beauty ... I am in little pain whether anybody chooses to follow the name I give them or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about scope: this work analyses origins and distinguishing qualities rather than attempting a complete taxonomy or exhaustive treatment of all aesthetic matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for classificatory adequacy: internal consistency and mutual opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the qualities which I have ranged under the head of the Sublime be all found consistent with each other, and all different from those which I place under the head of Beauty; and if those which compose the class of the Beautiful have the same consistency with themselves, and the same opposition to those which are classed under the denomination of Sublime ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grouping qualities under 'Sublime' or 'Beautiful', require that members cohere internally and stand in measurable opposition to the other class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty (listed as a primary topic in the inquiry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat novelty as a fundamental factor in considerations of taste and the sublime/beautiful; analyze how newness affects aesthetic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pain and Pleasure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how pain and pleasure contribute to aesthetic experience and how they differ in generating responses classified as sublime or beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between removal of pain and positive pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Difference between the Removal of Pain and Positive Pleasure (chapter focus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish relief-from-pain (negative pleasure) from active positive pleasure when analyzing aesthetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delight and Pleasure as opposed to each other
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Delight and Pleasure, as opposed to each other (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate subtle affective states—delight vs. pleasure—to clarify how different kinds of enjoyment relate to beauty and the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joy and Grief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the roles of joyful and grieving passions in aesthetic response, especially in tragic or sublime contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passions belonging to Self-Preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the Passions which belong to Self-Preservation (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how self-preservative passions (fear, terror, etc.) underpin certain sublime effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the Sublime (conceptual chapter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the Sublime (explicitly treated as its own chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a focused account of what qualifies as sublime, distinct from beauty, drawing on the other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passions which belong to Society
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the Passions which belong to Society (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine social passions (love, pride, emulation, etc.) and their relation to aesthetic responses categorized under beauty or the Sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cause of the difference between self-preservation passions and those regarding society of the sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Cause of the Difference between the Passions belonging to Self-Preservation, and those which regard the Society of the Sexes (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate why passions cluster differently according to their functional or teleological roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of Beauty (conceptual chapter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Beauty (explicitly treated as its own chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a focused account of what qualifies as beautiful, and how it differs structurally and affectively from the Sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society and Solitude
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how social context versus solitude affects perception of beauty and the Sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy, Imitation, and Ambition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these faculties together to explain communicative and imitative aspects of aesthetic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy (detailed chapter)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze sympathy's mechanisms and its effects on taste, emotion, and the reception of tragic or sublime works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of Sympathy in the Distresses of Others
rubrics_metrics.description: The Effects of Sympathy in the Distresses of Others (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how sympathetic responses to suffering are engaged aesthetically, especially in tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the Effects of Tragedy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the particular emotional dynamics enacted by tragedy and how they relate to sublime responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate imitation as a mechanism in art and rhetoric and its role in producing aesthetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss ambition as a motivating passion relevant to social and aesthetic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapitulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize and synthesize preceding analyses to show their mutual relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw final inferences about the origins of our ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the Passion caused by the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II topic: Of the Passion caused by the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the specific affective state or passion elicited by the Sublime as a distinct object of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terror
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze terror as a key ingredient in many sublime effects; distinguish it from ordinary fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscurity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how obscurity contributes to or heightens the sublime by withholding clear determination and provoking imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Clearness and Obscurity with regard to the Passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the Difference between Clearness and Obscurity with regard to the Passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the emotional consequences of clarity versus vagueness; determine when obscurity intensifies sublime passions and when clearness does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation on clearness/obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: [IV.] The Same Subject continued (further treatment of clearness/obscurity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the prior chapter's distinctions with further examples and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider perceived power or agency as a source of the sublime; analyze its rhetorical and imaginative manifestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore lack or deprivation as an aesthetic factor—how absence or negation can produce sublime effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vastness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat magnitude and spatial vastness as important contributors to feelings of the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how notions of the infinite—boundlessness, endlessness—stimulate sublime responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and Uniformity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at temporal and structural repetition or uniformity and their effects on awe or monotony in aesthetic experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude in Building
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine architectural scale and construction as sources of the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity in Pleasing Objects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how a sense of inexhaustibility or endlessness may contribute to pleasure in certain objects, and its relation to the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how challenge or perceived difficulty contributes to admiration or sublime feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnificence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat splendor, grandeur, and lavish display as aesthetic qualities tied to sublimity and social meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how illumination, contrasts of light and shade, and brightness influence sublime and beautiful perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light in Building
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on architectural uses of light to produce aesthetic effects—ambience, scale, mystery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color considered as productive of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Color considered as productive of the Sublime (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze which colors or color combinations tend to induce sublime impressions and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and Loudness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine auditory factors—volume, resonance, sudden loudness—as contributors to sublime affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suddenness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider abruptness and surprise as mechanisms that can produce or heighten sublime responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermitting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study intermittent phenomena—fluctuating stimuli—and their emotional/aesthetic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Cries of Animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vocal expressions in nature as examples for how raw sounds produce affective, sometimes sublime, responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smell and Taste—Bitters and Stenches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include olfactory and gustatory qualities in aesthetic analysis—how unpleasant or intense tastes/smells figure into feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling—Pain
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address bodily feeling, especially pain, and its complex relation to aesthetic reactions like the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of Beauty (Part III opening)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin dedicated, systematic treatment of beauty as distinct from the Sublime, with its own principles and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in Vegetables
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in Vegetables (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge simple proportionalist accounts of beauty by showing cases (vegetables) where proportion is not explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in Animals (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend the critique of proportion to animal forms—explain other factors that produce perceived beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in the Human Species
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion not the Cause of Beauty in the Human Species (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that human beauty cannot be reduced to mere proportion; explore alternative bases for judgments of human beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion further considered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more nuanced exploration of proportion's role—where it matters and where it fails as an explanatory principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness not the Cause of Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Fitness not the Cause of Beauty (chapter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject 'fitness' (functional appropriateness) as the primary explanation of beauty; consider the real effects of fitness separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Real Effects of Fitness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify what fitness does explain in aesthetic response, even if it is not the direct cause of beauty.
